newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Listless Australia stocks limp to lower close.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Listless Australia stocks limp to lower close.

text.p: The Australian share market ended a listless session marginally lower on Tuesday as traders found little inspiration from either local or offshore sources.
By 4.10 p.m. (0510 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 2.9 points lower at 2,419.4.
March share price index futures were down eight points at 2,435, a 15.6 point premium to the underlying index.

"It has been reasonably quiet," said David Iron, director of institutional sales at James Capel, adding that uncertainty about offshore markets had seen local traders hesitate before taking new positions.

"People have been watching the Dow which continues to do reasonably well. It recovered from a negative position towards the end of the day to claw its way into positive but the Japanese market is still giving people some grief," he said.
Local signals also remained elusive, despite healthy, if unspectacular, turnover.
"Volume hasn't been too bad, it's been a medium sort of day but issues in this market have been hard to come by," Iron said.
Advance Bank and Foster's Brewing headed turnover lists, accounting for about 15 percent of the day's turnover by value.

Advance Bank received final approval for its merger with fellow regional bank, St George Bank, sparking active trade as investors sought either to cash out or gain entry to the new A$4.5 billion entity.
Foster's Brewing also saw stong activity with brokers saying keen investor interest had driven the demand.

"There has been a lot of speculation around since pre-Christmas that there could be an unwinding of the BHP situation down the track," Iron said, noting that institutional investors expected BHP's 37.6 percent Fosters's stake to be dispersed widely rather than be sold in one line.
"A lot of institutions do expect the stock to be placed globally rather than a Heineken or the like coming in and taking it. It's certainly something people are watching out for."
Price-wise, the feature was Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting, whose shares jumped sharply as investors showed their approval of Monday's Sydney Harbour Casino bet.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about six to five, while about 31 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Options trade was lighter while futures trade slowed top a snail's pace with the lack of volatility.
Total options 24,843 (29,044)
Turnover in March SPI contracts totalled 2,363 (3,926).

In other local markets, Australian bonds finished up on the day, but just off their highs, after a solid start saw them rallying ahead of a A$600 million bond tender. Bonds eased slightly after the tender opened the afternoon trading session but still remained well supported, traders said. By 5.00 p.m. (0600 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.55 percent.

The Australian dollar stumbled below 78 cents Tuesday after the market suffered yet another bout of hysterics over domestic interest rates. By 5.00 pm (0600 GMT) the unit had found a fragile foothold at US$0.7778/83 down from US$0.7810/15 Monday.
